ITC Immunity Therapy Center - Alternative Cancer Treatment in Tijuana Profile Overview

Alternative Cancer Treatment at ITC Immunity Therapy Center

Navigating a cancer diagnosis can be overwhelming, prompting many individuals to explore innovative care pathways beyond standard protocols. Seeking Alternative Cancer Treatment in Tijuana, Mexico allows individuals to access customized medical modalities designed to stimulate the immune system and target malignant cells.

For individuals researching a cancer treatment clinic abroad, ITC provides compassionate, evidence-informed medical programs tailored to each individual's unique biological profile, medical history, and overall stage of diagnosis.

About ITC Immunity Therapy Center

Founded by Dr. Carlos Bautista, ITC - Immunity Therapy Center has established itself as a center focused on individualized care. Dr. Carlos Bautista brings decades of dedicated clinical research and medical leadership to the facility, prioritizing patient dignity, individualized care, and holistic biological preservation.

Located in Tijuana, Mexico—just minutes across the U.S. border—the center delivers progressive care pathways to international patients who are searching for alternative cancer treatment abroad in a modern, supportive medical setting.

How the Treatment Approach Works

Understanding how alternative cancer treatment works helps individuals navigate their healthcare options with clarity and confidence. At the core of the center's philosophy is immunity therapy cancer treatment, which combines therapies intended to support natural defenses while targeting malignant cells.

  • Initial Medical Review: Patients submit prior diagnosis reports, imaging results, blood tests, and medical history for detailed physician evaluation.

  • Individual Treatment Planning: A specialized care pathway is created based on the diagnosis, tumor location, biological health condition, and treatment goals.

  • Treatment Explanation: Physicians explain the objective of each therapy—such as laser therapy, hyperthermia, or biomagnetic therapy—ensuring patients understand the process and expected benefits.

  • Medical Monitoring: Daily clinical assessments and periodic blood tests track treatment response and manage side effects in real time.

  • Follow-Up Support: Post-treatment protocols, lifestyle advice, and continued communication guidance are provided for long-term recovery after returning home.

  • Coordination With Existing Doctors: Patients are encouraged to share medical updates with their home healthcare providers to maintain seamless medical care.

Treatment Eligibility and Patient Assessment

Evaluating eligibility for an integrative cancer treatment program involves a thorough review of medical records by qualified physicians. Candidacy depends on factors such as cancer type, stage, organ functionality, previous conventional treatments (chemotherapy or radiation), and current physical strength.

Whether exploring alternative treatment or complementary therapy alongside standard care, a structured medical evaluation determines whether the patient can safely participate in the program.

Risks and Important Medical Considerations

Evaluating cancer treatment decisions requires objective review of medical facts, individual diagnosis, and potential risks:

  • Cancer care outcomes vary based on individual biology, stage, and previous therapies.

  • Benefits and limitations of alternative therapies should be reviewed carefully prior to initiating treatment.

  • Possible side effects, detox reactions, or physical changes should be discussed with medical professionals.

  • Patients should avoid delaying necessary standard treatments without consulting their primary oncologist.

  • Seeking a second opinion can help patients make balanced, confident healthcare decisions.

Patient Travel and Support Services

ITC Immunity Therapy Center provides extensive logistical support for international visitors traveling to Tijuana, Mexico. The facility is located near San Diego International Airport (SAN), and dedicated shuttle services facilitate seamless border crossings and local transit to medical appointments and affiliated hotel accommodations.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is alternative cancer treatment at ITC Immunity Therapy Center?

Alternative cancer treatment at ITC refers to customized modalities—such as specialized immunotherapies, hyperthermia, and biomagnetic therapy—designed to support the immune system and target cancer cells. As a specialized cancer immunotherapy treatment center, ITC designs programs tailored to each patient's needs.

Who may be eligible for alternative cancer treatment at ITC Immunity Therapy Center?

Eligibility depends on cancer type, stage, physical strength, organ function, and medical history. Patients undergo a medical evaluation prior to acceptance.

How much does alternative cancer treatment at ITC Immunity Therapy Center cost?

Treatment costs start at $18,995 for standard multi-week programs. Total costs vary based on protocol duration, specific therapies required, and diagnostic needs.

Can alternative cancer treatment be combined with conventional cancer treatment?

Yes, many patients utilize integrative therapies alongside conventional treatments. Any combination should be coordinated with qualified physicians to evaluate safety and compatibility.

What risks should patients consider before choosing alternative cancer treatment?

Patients should consider potential side effects, detox responses, treatment limitations, and personal health conditions before starting therapy.

How do international patients arrange cancer treatment at ITC Immunity Therapy Center?

International patients submit medical records for review, receive a treatment plan and quote, and coordinate travel with ITC's support team.

What medical information should patients provide before consultation?

Patients should provide recent pathology reports, imaging scans (CT, MRI, PET), blood work, diagnosis summaries, and a history of previous treatments.

Sadie Litosky - HODGKIN LYMPHOMA

Sadie Litosky is a brave young girl from Canada. When Sadie was 19, she found out she was very sick with Hodgkin’s Lymphoma, a kind of cancer.

At first, she had a small bump on her neck, but then she started having trouble breathing and felt pain in her chest.

Sadie’s mom searched all over to find help. That’s when they found ITC.

Sadie was not sure about it at first, but she liked how ITC’s plan was gentle and would not hurt her body too much.

At ITC, Sadie got treatments that did not hurt a lot. After just two weeks, she felt better.

Her chest did not hurt anymore, she could breathe easily, and she had more energy. After three and a half months, her cancer was gone!

Sadie loved the kind nurses and doctors at ITC.

Dr. Bautista talked to her honestly, and everyone made her feel safe. Sadie said, “I was welcomed by everyone here, which was really nice, especially when I was scared.” ITC helped Sadie go from feeling scared to feeling hopeful and happy again.

Karla felt scared and sad, but she did nt give up hope. She went to ITC for help in May 2013.

At first, Karla’s son was not sure about ITC, but Karla believed it could help her.

When she got there, she saw how kind and caring everyone was. The treatments were gentle and did not hurt her body too much.

Karla liked how the doctors always told her what was happening and how she was getting better.

After three weeks of treatment at ITC in Mexico, Karla went back home.

She kept doing what the doctors told her, like eating healthy food and taking her medicine.

One day, Karla noticed the lumps on her breast were gone! She felt so happy and proud of herself.

Now, Karla does not need her oxygen tank or wheel chair anymore.

She can breathe and walk on her own. Karla knows there are still hard days, but she feels strong and free again.

Tijuana, Mexico Destination Overview

Medical Tourism for Cancer Treatment in Tijuana, Mexico

If you are thinking about going to Tijuana, Mexico, for cancer treatment, there is more to know than just the great doctors and hospitals. Tijuana is a fun and exciting city with many things to see and do.

It has good food, cool places to visit, and fun activities to enjoy while you are getting better. Let’s look at some of the best things to do in Tijuana and how you can get there easily.

Attractions worth Exploring

Tijuana is a fun place to visit! There are lots of cool things to see and do.

Walk Around: Go to Avenida Revolución! It has fun shops, yummy food, and pretty street art. It’s a great place to walk and look around.

Learn and Play: Visit the Tijuana Cultural Center! You can see art, watch plays, and learn about Mexico in a big IMAX theater.

Meet Wax People: The Tijuana Wax Museum has statues that look like real people! You can see famous people and learn about history in a fun way.

Eat Yummy Food: Try tacos, ceviche, and churros! The food here is super tasty and will make you happy.

Getting to Tijuana Made Easy

By Plane

San Diego International Airport (SAN) is just 25 minutes from Tijuana. Many people from the U.S., Canada, and other countries like this option. ITC even offers free rides to and from the airport.

By Plane

Tijuana also has its own airport, Tijuana International Airport (TIJ), with flights from many big U.S. cities. It’s a great choice for anyone coming for cancer treatment.

By Bus or Car

You can drive or take a bus to Tijuana if you’re in Mexico or the U.S. Highways connect Tijuana to big cities like San Diego, making it easy to get here by road.

By Train

If you’re in Southern California, trains like Amtrak’s Pacific Surfliner and the San Diego Trolley are good options. They’re a fun, green way to enjoy the trip to Tijuana.

Tijuana is a place where people can get help to feel better and also have fun! You can eat yummy food, see cool things, and meet nice people. No matter how you come—by plane, bus, car, or train—Tijuana is ready to welcome you and help you feel happy and healthy.

Reviews

Beware, the doctors lie to you at this clinic. I recently went down for 3 weeks of treatment for breast cancer. Even though I told them I didn't want their chemo treatment, they assured me it would be really helpful, they would only be using 10% and I would not lose my hair. They lied. I lost all of my hair which started 1 week after I returned home. When contacting my doctor he told me that was so unusual and recommended Minoxidal (which actually makes your hair shed worse before it regrows). This happened to 2 other women I kept in contact with. So it wasn't that unusual. When I followed up to find out what they gave me, it was the MOST toxic of all the chemotherapy treatments and they gave me a 50% dose, not 10%. It makes me question everything they are administering here. It has been extremely stressful which is opposite from what I need healing cancer. I am guessing they push chemo so much because they want results. I later found out the type of cancer I have, isn't responsive to chemotherapy. I would have hoped a clinic like this would have tests to check this. The total disrespect for me to make an informed decision makes me motivated to share my story to help protect others. I regret going here. Spend your money with doctors who are honest.

I will say that the nurses were spectacular. They deserve a 10 star rating. But the doctors deserve a -10 for taking advantage of their patients at their most vulnerable.

Guest P
